privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: {{app}} is an academic tool to document and present course projects (project-based learning). This notice explains which personal data it uses and how, under Colombian Law 1581 of 2012 and Decree 1377 of 2013.

sections.title: Who is responsible
body: The course teacher, who manages the tool and their class boards.

sections.title: Which data we use
body: From your Google account: name, email and profile photo. Your teacher also records your name and emails to add you to the board. If you choose, a photo you upload.
What you publish: your card's title and summary, the project stage you're in, your slides and the images you upload.
Technical security data: Google reCAPTCHA checks that requests come from this app.
Your votes in space polls: the teacher sees who voted; so does the poll’s author, unless it is anonymous.

Your class attendance (present, late, absent or excused, with an optional note by the teacher): your teacher records it; you see only yours (without the notes) and classmates never see it. Your teacher may copy your email to write to you from their own mail account, or email you from the app: emails go from your teacher's Gmail account (with Google's send-only permission), and the app keeps who each email went to and when, not its content.
Your sticky notes and reactions in classes: your teacher and every classmate on the board see them, with your name. Your teacher can move, edit or delete them.

Recorded classes play in YouTube's player in privacy-enhanced mode (youtube-nocookie.com); when a video plays, YouTube (Google) may set its own cookies. The app saves where you are in each class so you can pick up; your teacher sees which classes you watched, your classmates don't.

sections.title: What for
body: Only for the course: signing you in, showing your work to your teacher and to classmates on the same board, and presenting it in class. It is not sold, not used for advertising and not shared with anyone else.

sections.title: Who can see it
body: Your teacher and classmates on your board (read-only). Images are served through hard-to-guess links, but anyone with a link can see that image.

sections.title: Where it is stored
body: With third-party services that have their own security measures: Google Firebase (sign-in, database and website), Cloudinary (images) and Cloudflare (service that authorizes image uploads). Their servers may be outside Colombia (e.g. in the United States); by using the tool you authorize that transfer.
Content embedded in slides (Google, YouTube in privacy mode, Figma, Canva, Miro, Notion…) loads from each service’s servers when someone views the slide.

sections.title: For how long
body: As long as the course board exists. Unused boards move to “Archived projects” and the teacher can purge them: then your data, work and images are deleted.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can access, update, correct and ask to delete your data, and revoke this authorization, by writing to your teacher. If you get no answer, you can contact Colombia's Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC).

embeds.guideTitle: How to embed content in your slides
embeds.guideIntro: In the editor use “Insert content” and paste the link. For everyone to see it, the file must be shared as shown below.

providers.googleSlides: Share → General access: “Anyone with the link” (Viewer) → Copy link. File → Share → Publish to the web also works.
providers.googleDocs: Share → “Anyone with the link” (Viewer) → Copy link.
providers.googleSheets: Share → “Anyone with the link” (Viewer) → Copy link.
providers.googleForms: Send → link icon → Copy. The form can be answered from the slide.
providers.googleDrive: Right-click the file (video or PDF) → Share → “Anyone with the link” → Copy link.
providers.youtube: Copy the video link (public or unlisted). It plays in privacy mode (no tracking cookies).
providers.vimeo: Copy the video link; its settings must allow embedding on other sites.
providers.figma: Share → “Anyone with the link” → “can view” → Copy link. Works for designs, prototypes, FigJam and Figma Slides.
providers.canva:
Option 1 · Link: Share → Access: “Anyone with the link” (can view) → Copy link.
Option 2 · Code: Share → Embed (or “More” → Embed) → Embed → Copy the HTML code.
Edit links and short links (canva.link) work too; the design keeps its real shape (portrait, square or 16:9).
providers.miro: Share → “Anyone with the board link” → “can view” → Copy board link.
providers.notion: Share → Publish → Publish to web → copy the link ending in notion.site.
providers.prezi: Share → Share public link (view) → Copy link.
providers.padlet: Share → “Embed in your blog or website” → copy the address that contains /embed/.
